Joseph dreams that eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrate to him; his father tells him to keep it from his brothers and says his Lord will choose him.
Saying their father loves Joseph more, his brothers put him in a well and claim a wolf ate him; travelers find him, and he is sold for a few dirhams.
Bought by a man from Egypt, Joseph reaches maturity; the man's wife tries to seduce him, he refuses, and his shirt torn from the back shows she lied.
Women of the city blame al-'Azeez's wife; at her banquet they cut their hands on seeing Joseph; he prefers prison to their invitation and is imprisoned for a time.
Two prisoners ask Joseph to interpret their dreams; he calls them to worship Allah alone, says one will serve wine and one be crucified, and stays imprisoned several years.
The eminent ones cannot interpret the king's dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean; Joseph foretells seven years of planting, seven difficult years, then a year of rain.
The king summons Joseph, who asks about the women who cut their hands; al-'Azeez's wife admits she sought to seduce him, and Joseph asks to oversee the land's storehouses.
Joseph's brothers come to him without recognizing him; he tells them to bring their brother from their father, who demands their promise by Allah to bring him back.
Joseph tells his brother who he is and puts the king's measure in his bag; accused of theft, the brothers set the penalty, and Joseph keeps his brother.
Told his son has stolen, Jacob grieves for Joseph until his eyes whiten and sends his sons to seek him; Joseph reveals himself and forgives his brothers.
Joseph sends his shirt; Jacob finds Joseph's smell and regains sight from the shirt; the family enter Egypt, his parents prostrate to Joseph, and his earlier vision is fulfilled.
